sentences.en: If you type in the words left brain versus right brain on YouTube,
sentences.zh: 如果你在YouTube上搜索左脑与右脑这两个词，

sentences.en: it's not long before you'll find yourself in a vortex of weird claims and outlandish hype.
sentences.zh: 你很快就会陷入奇谈怪论和离奇炒作的漩涡之中。

sentences.en: With the left brain imbalance, the overall function of the brain is stunted
sentences.zh: 如果左脑失衡，大脑的整体功能就会受阻，

sentences.en: so that the oldest part of the brain, the reptile brain, takes over on an instinctual level.
sentences.zh: 从而使大脑中最古老的部分——爬虫脑，在直觉层面接管一切。

sentences.en: We need systeMs. That's the left brain, by the way, for men.
sentences.zh: 我们需要系统。顺便说一句，对男人来说，这就是左脑。

sentences.en: Now the problem is that most people are either exclusively left-brained or right-brained.
sentences.zh: 问题是，大多数人要么完全是左脑型，要么完全是右脑型。

sentences.en: For decades, pop psychology books and plenty of YouTube videos
sentences.zh: 几十年来，通俗心理学书籍和大量的YouTube视频

sentences.en: have made dramatic claims about people who are left-brained and people who are right-brained.
sentences.zh: 对左脑型的人和右脑型的人做出了耸人听闻的断言。

sentences.en: It got to the point that respectable scientists felt they had to steer clear of the study of hemispheric differences.
sentences.zh: 甚至到了受人尊敬的科学家觉得必须避开半球差异研究的地步。

sentences.en: I was told when I got involved in this area, don't touch it.
sentences.zh: 当我涉足这个领域时，别人告诉我，不要碰它。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we follow the work of a researcher who went there.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐形大脑》节目中，我们将关注一位涉足该领域的钻研者的工作。

sentences.en: What he's found is much more nuanced and complex than the story on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 他所发现的东西比YouTube上的说法要微妙和复杂得多。

sentences.en: His conclusions, though, might be even more dramatic.
sentences.zh: 不过，他的结论可能更加震撼。

sentences.en: He argues that differences in the brain and Western society's preference for what one hemisphere has to offer
sentences.zh: 他认为，大脑的差异以及西方社会对某一半球功能的偏爱，

sentences.en: have had enormous effects on our lives.
sentences.zh: 对我们的生活产生了巨大的影响。
伊恩·麦基尔克里斯是一位精神病学家。

sentences.en: He has spent years studying the human brain through case studies of his patients
sentences.zh: 他通过对病人的个案研究

sentences.en: and a detailed examination of scientific research.
sentences.zh: 以及对科学研究的详细考察，花费了多年时间研究人脑。

sentences.en: He's found himself fascinated with a question that has intrigued philosophers and scientists for centuries.
sentences.zh: 他发现自己对一个几个世纪以来一直让哲学家和科学家着迷的问题深深吸引。

sentences.en: Why is the human brain divided in half?
sentences.zh: 为什么人脑要一分为二？

sentences.en: How does each hemisphere shape our perceptions?
sentences.zh: 每个半球是如何塑造我们的认知的？

sentences.en: Ian's book on this topic has been on my radar for many years.
sentences.zh: 伊恩关于这个主题的书我关注很多年了。

sentences.en: It's called The Master and His Emissary.
I asked him to start with a basic overview of what the two hemispheres do.
sentences.zh: 我请他先对这两个半球的功能做一个基本的概述。

sentences.en: In motor terms, it's fairly straightforward that the left hemisphere controls the right side of the body
sentences.zh: 从运动机能上讲，左半球控制身体右侧

sentences.en: and receives messages from it and vice versa.
sentences.zh: 并接收来自右侧的信息，反之亦然，这相当直接。

sentences.en: But in terms of psychological life, they have quite different kinds of roles.
sentences.zh: 但在心理生活方面，它们扮演着截然不同的角色。
它们有着截然不同的性格倾向。

sentences.en: And I believe evolutionarily, they are, if you like, addressing different questions.
sentences.zh: 而且我相信，从进化角度来说，如果你愿意的话，它们是在解决不同的问题。

sentences.en: If you look at the last 20 or 30 years, Ian, there's been a lot of work or speculation, really,
sentences.zh: 如果你看看过去二十或三十年，伊恩，确实有很多关于这两个半球在感知和行为方面如何运作的工作或推测。

sentences.en: looking at how these two hemispheres might operate when it comes to perception, when it comes to behavior.
sentences.zh: 你在这本书中认为，对于这两个半球如何运作以及它们的不同角色是什么，存在着许多过度简化的观点。

sentences.en: You argue in the book that there have been many oversimplifications of how the two hemispheres work
and what their different roles are.
sentences.zh: 这种过度简化的世界是什么样的？
好吧，传统模型大概是在60年代和70年代兴起的，

sentences.en: What does this world of oversimplification look like?
sentences.zh: 在80年代甚至90年代还有一定的影响力，

sentences.en: Well, the conventional model is something that sprang up probably in the 60s and 70s
sentences.zh: 而现在可能主要存在于中层管理培训项目和通俗心理学书籍中。

sentences.en: and had some life into the 80s and even into the 90s
and is now probably mainly at home in middle management programs and pop psychology books.
sentences.zh: 别人告诉我，不要碰它，它有毒，甚至不要去想。

sentences.en: And I was told when I got involved in this area,
sentences.zh: 基本上就是说左半球是逻辑和语言性的，

sentences.en: don't touch it, it's toxic, don't even go there.
sentences.zh: 而右半球有点情绪化，可能还有点创造力。

sentences.en: And basically that was that the left hemisphere is logical and verbal
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，这一切要复杂得多，其中有些甚至是完全错误的。

sentences.en: and that the right hemisphere is kind of moody and possibly creative.
sentences.zh: 当我们审视大脑的进化时，不仅在人类中，在其他物种中也是如此，

sentences.en: But all of this turns out to be much more complicated and some of it's plain wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们在其他物种身上也能发现类似的划分吗？

sentences.en: When we look at the evolution of the brain, not just among humans but other species,
do we find a similar division in other species?

sentences.zh: 它存在于所有哺乳动物、两栖动物、爬行动物、鱼类、昆虫、线虫中，

sentences.en: This is not something that was invented by human beings.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其中一种线虫有302个神经元，但它是不对称运作的。

sentences.en: It's there in all mammals, amphibians, reptiles, fish, insects, nematode worms,
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们所知的拥有任何形式神经网络的最古老生物

sentences.en: which have, you know, like one of them has 302 neurons, but it's working asymmetrically.
And in fact, the oldest creature that we know of that has a neural net of any kind

sentences.zh: 它被认为是神经网络的起源。

sentences.en: And it's thought of as the origin of neural networks.
sentences.zh: 这个神经网络是不对称的。
所以在某种程度上，这确实引发了一个问题：为什么大脑要被划分开来，对吧？
我的意思是，这确实是个问题。

sentences.en: And so in some ways, this does prompt the question, why would you have the brain be divided, right?
sentences.zh: 它当然是个问题，特别是如果你赞同——而我坚决不赞同——大脑是一台计算机这种观点的话。

sentences.en: I mean, it does beg the question.
sentences.zh: 因为如果是那样，把大脑分成两部分绝对是对计算能力的巨大浪费。

sentences.en: It certainly begs the question, particularly if you buy, which I emphatically don't,
sentences.zh: 如果你去古董店，你可能会发现海报上面画着一个人头，大脑像地图一样被划分开来。

sentences.en: the idea that the brain is a computer.
sentences.zh: 理性在一个象限，情感在另一个象限。

sentences.en: Because if it is, surely it's a vast waste of computing power to have this brain divided into two bits.
sentences.zh: 记忆在这边，想象力在那里。

sentences.en: If you go to an antique store, you might find posters showing a human head with the brain divided like a map.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，对半球差异的通俗描绘都集中在头脑不同部分的功能上。

sentences.en: Reason is in one quadrant, emotion in another.
sentences.zh: 伊恩说，真正区别两个半球的不是它们做什么，

sentences.en: Memory is over here, imagination there.
sentences.zh: 而是它们如何以不同的方式做同样的事情。

sentences.en: For a long time, the popular representations of hemispheric differences focused on what different parts of the brain do.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，我们之所以弄错，是因为我们只是简单地看待我们所看到的功能，

sentences.en: Ian says what really distinguishes the hemispheres is not what they do,
sentences.zh: 并按照我们思考机器的方式将它们划分开来。

sentences.en: but how they do the same things differently.
sentences.zh: 机器的这一部分做这个。

sentences.en: The reason that we got things wrong, in my view, is that we were looking at simply the functions as we saw them
sentences.zh: 机器的那一部分做那个。

sentences.en: and divided them up in much the way that we would if we thought about a machine.
sentences.zh: 如果你不使用机器模型，而是使用“这是人类、是个人的一部分”这一模型，

sentences.en: This part of the machine does this.
sentences.zh: 你就会问一个稍微不同的问题，不仅是它做什么，还有它是怎么做的？

sentences.en: This part of the machine does that.
sentences.zh: 在观察大脑半球时，这被证明是一个意义深远的重要问题，

sentences.en: And if you, instead of using the machine model, use the model of this is part of a human being, a person,
sentences.zh: 因为它们都参与了每一项活动。

sentences.en: you would ask a slightly different question, which is not just what does it do, but how does it do it?
And that turns out to be a profoundly important question when looking at the hemispheres,
sentences.zh: 这就是，相当一致地，每个半球都以完全不同的方式做所有这些事情，

sentences.en: because they are both involved in doing everything.
sentences.zh: 带着一种不同的精神，走向不同的目标，如果你愿意这样表述的话。
伊恩认为大脑分为两个半球，这样它就能产生对现实的两种不同看法。

sentences.en: It's that quite consistently, each hemisphere does all these things in a totally different way,
sentences.zh: 其中一个半球，即右半球，专注于全局。

sentences.en: with a different kind of spirit towards a different end, if you like to put it that way.
Ian believes the brain is divided into two hemispheres, so that it can produce two different views of reality.
One of the hemispheres, the right, focuses on the big picture.
sentences.zh: 如果你看不到全局，你就不会明白自己在做什么。
如果你不能聚焦于细节，你就无法完成最简单的任务。
事实证明，这种方向上的根本差异对两个半球所做的一切都有着深远的影响。

sentences.en: If you can't see the big picture, you don't understand what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 伊恩以学习一首曲子为例来解释这是如何运作的。

sentences.en: If you can't home in on the details, you can't accomplish the simplest tasks.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，你被一首曲子吸引了，你试着完整地弹奏它，你很喜欢它。

sentences.en: This fundamental difference in orientation turns out to have profound consequences for everything the two hemispheres do.
sentences.zh: 但你意识到有些地方你没有弹对。

sentences.en: Ian uses the example of learning a piece of music to explain how this works.
sentences.zh: 所以你知道你需要练习第18小节的指法。

sentences.en: Imagine you are attracted to a piece of music, and you try playing it as a whole, and you love it.
sentences.zh: 当你把它拆解时，你意识到，哦，这里我们转到了下属音。

sentences.en: But you realize that there are bits that you're not getting right.
sentences.zh: 此时，我们正在回到属音。

sentences.en: So you know you need to practice your fingering at bar 18.
sentences.zh: 你理解了大量的细节，这很好。

sentences.en: And when you're taking it apart, you realize, oh, here we move into the subdominant.
sentences.zh: 你需要去做这些功课，你需要做分析。

sentences.en: At this point, we're moving back to the dominant.
sentences.zh: 但当你真正开始演奏这首曲子时，你必须把所有这些抛诸脑后。

sentences.en: You understand a whole lot of details, which are fine.
sentences.zh: 否则，你将无法完整地演奏它。

sentences.en: You need to do the work, and you need to do the analysis.
sentences.zh: 右半球在开始时把握全局。

sentences.en: But when you come to play the piece, you must put all that out of your mind.
sentences.zh: 左半球将其拆解并丰富它。

sentences.en: Otherwise, you won't be able to play it all.
sentences.zh: 但是这项工作完成后，它需要被带回整体的画面中，

sentences.en: The right hemisphere takes in the whole at the start.
sentences.zh: 而这只有右半球才能做到。

sentences.en: The left hemisphere unpacks that and enriches it.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这当然不仅限于你学习一首音乐作品的时候。

sentences.en: But then that work being done, it needs to be taken back into the whole picture,
sentences.zh: 你在书中有大量的案例，

sentences.en: which only the right hemisphere can do.
sentences.zh: 包括在动物界中，当一只鸟试图去啄一粒谷物时，

sentences.en: And it seems to me that this is not just, of course, when you're learning a piece of music.
sentences.zh: 它实际上需要同时做两件不同的事情。

sentences.en: You have examples in the book of numerous cases,
sentences.zh: 所有的生物都需要能够以两种不同的方式关注世界，

sentences.en: including in the animal world, when a bird is trying to pick up a grain of corn,
sentences.zh: 这需要在同一时间投入截然不同的注意力。

sentences.en: it actually needs to be doing two different things at once.
sentences.zh: 除非它们能够相对独立地运作，否则这是绝对不可能的。

sentences.en: All living creatures need to be able to attend to the world in two different ways,
sentences.zh: 一方面，为了操纵世界、获取食物、捡树枝、筑巢，

sentences.en: which require quite different attention at the same time.
sentences.zh: 你需要对细节进行非常精确、有针对性的关注，以便能够实现这一目标

sentences.en: And this is simply not possible unless they can work relatively independently.
On the one hand, in order to manipulate the world, to get food, to pick up a twig, to build a nest,
sentences.zh: 但如果你只做这件事，如果你是一只只专注于小种子的鸟，

sentences.en: you need a very precise targeted attention on a detail in order to be able to achieve that
sentences.zh: 你在获取自己食物的同时，就会成为别人午餐的对象，

sentences.en: and be ahead of your competition.
sentences.zh: 因为你需要同时投入截然相反的注意力，

sentences.en: But if you're only doing that, if you're a bird just concentrating on the little seed,
sentences.zh: 不是支离破碎、狭隘琐碎和完全细节化的注意力，

sentences.en: you'll become somebody else's lunch while you're getting your own,
sentences.zh: 而是持续、广阔且对捕食者以及同类保持警惕的注意力。

sentences.en: because you need, at the same time, to be paying the precise opposite kind of attention,
sentences.zh: 几十年前，科学家发现这两个半球是由一束神经纤维连接起来的。

sentences.en: not piecemeal, fragmented, and entirely detailed,
sentences.zh: 他们将其命名为胼胝体。

sentences.en: but sustained broad and vigilant for predators and for other members of your species.
sentences.zh: 胼胝体通常被描述为一座桥梁，

sentences.en: Decades ago, scientists discovered that the two hemispheres are connected by a bundle of nerve fibers.
sentences.zh: 它在两个半球之间传递信息。

sentences.en: They named it the corpus callosum.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，它更像是一个交通信号灯。

sentences.en: The corpus callosum is often described as a bridge
sentences.zh: 为了进行协作，你们既需要共同工作，也需要各自独立工作。

sentences.en: that it passes information back and forth between the hemispheres.
sentences.zh: 如果外科医生与器械护士合作，他们不会两个人都去干同一份工作。

sentences.en: But it turns out, it is much more like a traffic signal.
In order to collaborate, you need to both work together and work separately.
sentences.zh: 胼胝体既能实现分离——我认为主要是分离，也能实现连接。

sentences.en: If a surgeon collaborates with the scrub nurse, they don't both try and do the same job.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太不可思议了，不是吗？
当你想到这一点时，看起来我们的脑袋里确实有两个不同的大脑。

sentences.en: And the corpus callosum enables both separation, mainly, I believe, separation, but also connection.
sentences.zh: 当然，第一批研究裂脑患者的人认为那里有两个不同的人，

sentences.en: I mean, that's extraordinary, isn't it?
When you think about this, it really looks like we actually have two different brains inside our head.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些都是神经病学和神经心理学史上的著名人物。

sentences.en: Certainly, the first people to look at split-brain patients thought that there were two distinct people there,
sentences.zh: 他们会把这两个半球谈论为两个人。

sentences.en: and they would talk to one another.
sentences.zh: 伊恩的书包含了很多科学内容，但它也是对现代工业社会的评论。

sentences.en: I mean, these are very famous names in the history of neurology, neuropsychology.
sentences.zh: 书名来自一个寓言，一个关于统治一片土地的明智的精神主人的神话。

sentences.en: They would talk about the two hemispheres as two people.
sentences.zh: 而这个使者虽然精明，但还不够精明，不知道自己不知道什么。

sentences.en: Ian's book has a lot of science in it, but it's also a commentary on modern industrial societies.
The title of the book comes from a parable, a myth about a wise, spiritual master who rules over a land.
sentences.zh: 他心想，主人算什么，当我在做所有苦差事时，他却坐在那里神圣地微笑着。

sentences.en: And this emissary was bright enough, but not quite bright enough to know what it was he didn't know.
sentences.zh: 于是他披上了主人的斗篷，假装自己是主人。

sentences.en: And he thought, I know everything.
sentences.zh: 因为他不知道自己不知道什么，结果导致整个社区基本上崩溃了。

sentences.en: And he thought, what does the master know, sitting back there seraphically smiling while I do all the hard work.
sentences.zh: 伊恩认为，大脑的右半球应该扮演我们精神王国的明智主人的角色。

sentences.en: And so he adopted the master's cloak, pretended to be the master.
sentences.zh: 左半球应该是那个使者。

sentences.en: And because he didn't know what he didn't know, the result was that the community fell apart, essentially.
sentences.zh: 伊恩说，我们已经对使者的技能迷恋不已。

sentences.en: Ian argues that the right hemisphere of the brain is supposed to play the role of the wise master of our mental kingdom.
sentences.zh: 我们珍视细节，却对宏观全局不屑一顾。

sentences.en: The left hemisphere is supposed to be the emissary.
sentences.zh: 他用一个类比来形容两个半球之间的关系。

sentences.en: Ian says we have grown infatuated with the skills of the emissary.
sentences.zh: 我想强调的是，我强烈反对大脑是一台计算机这种观点。

sentences.en: We prize the details, but scorn the big picture.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它一点也不像计算机。

sentences.en: He makes an analogy about the relationship between the hemispheres.
sentences.zh: 但在一个有限的意义上，左半球有点像一台非常非常聪明的计算机。

sentences.en: I want to emphasize that I resist very strongly the idea that the brain is a computer.
sentences.zh: 而这正是它变得危险的地方。

sentences.en: It's just nothing like a computer, actually.
sentences.zh: 它是一台非常非常聪明的计算机，

sentences.en: But in this one limited sense, the left hemisphere is a little bit like a very, very smart computer.
sentences.zh: 但它却不知道自己不知道什么。

sentences.en: So you know what the data that you've collected mean, but you haven't yet been able to analyze them.
sentences.zh: 所以你知道你所收集的数据意味着什么，但你还没能对它们进行分析。

sentences.en: You put them into a machine that is just very clever at carrying out a routine.
sentences.zh: 你把它们输入一台非常擅长执行常规任务的机器中。

sentences.en: And then it spews out a result, which it also doesn't understand.
sentences.zh: 然后它吐出一个结果，它同样也不理解。

sentences.en: But you then take back into the world where the data come from and go, I see.
sentences.zh: 但随后你将结果带回数据诞生的世界，心想：原来如此。
这就是它们之间的关系。

sentences.en: Your left hemisphere is busy processing things to make sure they're consistent and unpacked.
sentences.zh: 你的左半球正忙于处理各种事务，以确保它们保持一致且被妥善梳理。

sentences.en: But your right hemisphere is seeing everything.
sentences.zh: 但你的右半球却在观察一切。

sentences.en: I'm suggesting that we have arrived at a place, not for the first time in the West,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在西方已经走到了这样一个地步——这并非第一次——

sentences.en: where we have slipped into listening only to what it is that the left hemisphere can tell us
sentences.zh: 我们不知不觉地只去倾听左半球所能告诉我们的东西，

sentences.en: and discounting what the right hemisphere could have told us.
sentences.zh: 而忽视了右半球本可以告诉我们的内容。

sentences.en: And in your analogy here, the right hemisphere is the master.
sentences.zh: 在你这里的比喻中，右半球是主人。

sentences.en: The left hemisphere is the emissary.
In my interpretation of that myth, that's right, yeah.
sentences.zh: 在我对那个神话的解读中，确实如此。

sentences.en: Coming up, we look more closely at Ian's view that we're living in a left hemisphere world.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们将深入探讨伊恩的观点，即我们正生活在一个左半球的世界里。

sentences.en: And we dive into the ways the left and right hemispheres produce different accounts of reality.
sentences.zh: 我们还将探讨左右半球对现实产生不同诠释的方式。

sentences.en: In 1997, PBS aired a documentary about a patient named Joe.
sentences.zh: 1997年，公共广播电视公司（PBS）播放了一部关于一位名叫乔的病人的纪录片。

sentences.en: I was having seizures like every day.
So there's two or three a day.
sentences.zh: 所以一天会有两到三次。

sentences.en: Joe's doctors devised a treatment that sounded more sci-fi than like a real medical procedure.
sentences.zh: 乔的医生设计了一种听起来更像是科幻小说而不是真实医疗程序的治疗方法。

sentences.en: A surgeon literally split his brain in two.
sentences.zh: 外科医生活生生地把他的大脑一分为二。

sentences.en: The surgeon sliced the corpus callosum, the nerve fibers that connect the left and right hemispheres.
sentences.zh: 外科医生切开了胼胝体，即连接左右半球的神经纤维。

sentences.en: In Joe's case, the surgery accomplished what the doctors hoped.
sentences.zh: 就乔的情况而言，这次手术实现了医生们的期望。

sentences.en: I know the left hemisphere and the right hemisphere now are working independent of each other.
sentences.zh: 我知道左右半球现在是彼此独立工作的。
但你并不会察觉到这一点。

sentences.en: Now, you just kind of adapt to it.
sentences.zh: 现在，你只是有点适应了它。

sentences.en: It doesn't, you don't have any feeling, it doesn't feel any different than it did before.
sentences.zh: 它不会……你没有任何感觉，感觉和以前没有任何区别。

sentences.en: Psychiatrist Ian McGilchrist says many other patients with epilepsy have been helped by this procedure.
sentences.zh: 精神病学家伊恩·麦克吉尔克里斯特表示，许多其他癫痫患者也通过这一手术获得了帮助。
zh_words: 伊恩·麦克吉尔克里斯特

sentences.en: So by simply separating the two hemispheres so that an electrical storm, if you like, in one hemisphere couldn't cross over and invade the other,
sentences.zh: 因此，通过简单地将两个半球分隔开，使得一个半球内的电风暴（如果你愿意这么说的话）无法跨越并侵入另一个半球，

sentences.en: they were able actually to carry on a remarkably normal life.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上能够过上非常正常的生活。

sentences.en: So this was a life-saving procedure.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一次挽救生命的手术。

sentences.en: But it also had the consequence that by clever experimentation, you could deliver information to one hemisphere at a time
sentences.zh: 但它也带来了一个结果：通过巧妙的实验，你可以一次向一个半球传递信息，

sentences.en: and find out what that hemisphere knew and had to say about it.
sentences.zh: 并找出那个半球对该信息了解多少以及有何看法。

sentences.en: These experiments showed the left and right hemisphere approach everyday tasks very differently.
sentences.zh: 这些实验表明，左右半球对待日常任务的方式截然不同。

sentences.en: The left focuses on narrow details, the right on general vigilance.
sentences.zh: 左半球专注于细枝末节，右半球则关注整体的警觉性。

sentences.en: To use a basketball analogy, the left hemisphere is focused on the mechanics of dunking the basketball.
sentences.zh: 用篮球来打个比方，左半球专注于扣篮的技术动作。

sentences.en: The right, on where all the players are, the current situation in the game.
sentences.zh: 右半球则关注所有球员的位置以及比赛的当前局势。

sentences.en: You see something similar when it comes to language.
sentences.zh: 当涉及语言时，你也会看到类似的情况。

sentences.en: One of them is attending to the tone of voice in which I say something.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是关注我说话时的语调。

sentences.en: For example, I can say, yes, or I can say, yes.
sentences.zh: 例如，我可以说是，或者我可以说是。

sentences.en: I can intone that in probably a dozen different ways with quite different meanings.
sentences.zh: 我可以带着大概十几种不同的语气来读这个词，它们的意思截然不同。

sentences.en: So, for example, I say, it's a bit hot in here.
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，我说，这里有点热。

sentences.en: You using your right hemisphere know that what I mean is, could we have the door open?
sentences.zh: 运用右半球的你听出我的意思是：我们能把门打开吗？

sentences.en: Could we put on the air conditioning?
But your left hemisphere is wondering, meanwhile, why I'm supplying this quite unnecessary meteorological information.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，你的左半球却在纳闷，为什么我要提供这些完全没有必要的气象信息。

sentences.en: So it's really focused on sort of the granular detail.
sentences.zh: 所以它真的非常专注于那种细枝末节。

sentences.en: Yes, and because of this, all kinds of things happen.
sentences.zh: 是的，正因为如此，各种各样的事情都会发生。

sentences.en: Because of its narrow focus, it doesn't see anything that isn't explicit.
sentences.zh: 由于它那狭隘的专注，它看不到任何并非显式表达的东西。

sentences.en: It only sees what's right in the center of the focus of attention.
sentences.zh: 它只能看到注意力焦点正中央的内容。

sentences.en: And it doesn't understand things that are not said.
sentences.zh: 并且它无法理解那些未曾说出口的话语。

sentences.en: Often, that's as important as what is said.
sentences.zh: 通常，言外之意和言内之意同样重要。

sentences.en: The way in which it is said, my facial expression, my body language, all of this is lost,
sentences.zh: 说话的方式、我的面部表情、我的肢体语言，所有这些都丢失了，

sentences.en: as well as the interpretation in the whole picture.
sentences.zh: 对宏观全景的解读也是如此。

sentences.en: One of the important differences you point out is sort of understanding the role of metaphor in language, for example,
sentences.zh: 你指出的一个重要区别在于理解语言中隐喻的作用，例如，

sentences.en: which is that the left hemisphere really is incapable of understanding what metaphor is or how it works.
sentences.zh: 左半球实际上完全无法理解什么是隐喻或隐喻是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Yes, and that's no small thing.
Because as some philosophers have pointed out, metaphor is how we understand everything.
sentences.zh: 正如一些哲学家所指出的，隐喻是我们理解一切的方式。

sentences.en: And they point out that actually particularly scientific and philosophical understanding is mediated by metaphors.
sentences.zh: 他们指出，实际上尤其是科学和哲学的理解都是以隐喻为媒介的。

sentences.en: In other words, the only way we can understand something is in terms of something else that we think we already understand.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们理解某事物的唯一方式，是通过我们自认为已经理解的另一事物来加以理解。

sentences.en: And it's making the analogy, which is what a metaphor does, that enables us to go, I see, I get it.
sentences.zh: 正是这种类比——这正是隐喻所做的事情——让我们能够说：我明白了，我懂了。

sentences.en: Now, if you think that metaphor is just one of those dispensable decorations that you could add to meaning,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你认为隐喻只是可以为意义增色的那些可有可无的装饰，

sentences.en: it's kind of nice, but probably a distraction from the real meaning.
sentences.zh: 觉得它挺美，但可能分散了对真正含义的注意力，

sentences.en: You've got it upside down, because if you don't understand the metaphor, you haven't understood the meaning.
sentences.zh: 那你就大错特错了，因为如果你不理解隐喻，你就没有真正理解含义。

sentences.en: Literal meaning, however, is a peripheral diminished version of the richness of metaphorical understanding.
sentences.zh: 然而，字面意义只是丰富隐喻理解的一种边缘化、缩水版本的体现。

sentences.en: And what we know is the right hemisphere understands those implicit meanings, those connections of meanings,
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，右半球能够理解那些隐含的意义、意义之间的联系，

sentences.en: what we call connotations, as well as just denotations.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们所说的内涵，以及字面外延。

sentences.en: It understands imagery, it understands humor, it understands all of that.
sentences.zh: 它理解意象，它理解幽默，它理解所有这些。

sentences.en: Do the hemispheres differ in how they think about time, their orientation towards the future and their orientation toward the past?
sentences.zh: 左右半球在对时间的思考方式上、在面向未来的导向和面向过去的导向方面有所不同吗？

sentences.en: Well, that's an interesting question, and not in a clear-cut way,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个有趣的问题，但并非一种非黑即白的方式，

sentences.en: although the left hemisphere is tending to look for the next opportunity,
sentences.zh: 尽管左半球倾向于寻找下一个机会，

sentences.en: so it's very goal-driven, but very short-term goal-driven.
sentences.zh: 所以它非常具有目标导向性，但注重的是非常短期的目标导向。

sentences.en: It wants to grasp things that are within reach.
sentences.zh: 它想要抓住触手可及的东西。

sentences.en: Remember, the left hemisphere is what controls our right hand,
sentences.zh: 记住，左半球控制着我们的右手，

sentences.en: with which we grasp things that are within reach.
sentences.zh: 我们用右手去抓取触手可及的事物。

sentences.en: So it has a very direct, linear idea of a target, and let's go and get it.
sentences.zh: 因此，它对目标有着非常直接、线性的概念，那就是去把目标拿过来。

sentences.en: Is some of this played out in sort of the relationship they have with tradition, with history, as you say?
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，其中一部分是否体现在它们与传统、与历史的关系中？

sentences.en: And in some ways, if I'm primarily focused on what's right in front of me,
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，如果我主要关注眼前的东西，

sentences.en: I don't really need to know what the last 2,000 years of history have taught me.
sentences.zh: 我其实不需要知道过去两千年的历史教给了我什么。
我认为这绝对是正确的。

sentences.en: Time can be seen rather like the flow of a river,
sentences.zh: 时间可以被看作就像河流的流动，

sentences.en: which isn't made up of slices or chunks of river that are then put together.
sentences.zh: 它并不是由一块块或一片片拼凑起来的河流切片组成的。

sentences.en: We as personalities in time, our cultures in time, are like this flow.
sentences.zh: 我们作为时间中的个体，我们在时间中的文化，就像这种流动一样。

sentences.en: The left hemisphere can't deal with anything that is moving.
sentences.zh: 左半球无法处理任何处于运动中的事物。

sentences.en: It likes things to be fixed because then you can grab them.
sentences.zh: 它喜欢把事物固定，因为那样你就能抓住它们。

sentences.en: You can't pick up something unless you can at least immobilize it for that second while you're interacting with it.
sentences.zh: 除非你至少能在与之交互的那一秒钟内将猎物定格，否则你什么也捡不起来。

sentences.en: So it doesn't like flow and motion, which are, in my view, basic to not just life, but actually to the cosmos.
sentences.zh: 所以它不喜欢流动和运动，在我看来，流动和运动不仅是生命的基础，实际上也是整个宇宙的基础。

sentences.en: So instead, it sees lots of little punctate moments, little slices of time,
sentences.zh: 因此，它看到的不是流动，而是许多微小的离散瞬间、时间的切片，

sentences.en: and things have to be put together by adding them up.
sentences.zh: 并且这些事物必须通过将它们相加来拼凑在一起。

sentences.en: I mean, it's almost like a form of calculus, you know, of taking slices and then trying to integrate them together.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这几乎就像是一种微积分的形式，你知道的，就是截取切片，然后试图将它们整合在一起。

sentences.en: And calculus is an attempt, actually, to achieve something which is indivisible by dividing it into slices.
sentences.zh: 而微积分实际上就是一种尝试，试图通过将不可分割的事物划分成切片来达成某种目标。

sentences.en: The two hemispheres even appear to have different value systeMs.
sentences.zh: 这两个半球甚至似乎拥有不同的价值体系。

sentences.en: The left hemisphere prefers to reduce moral questions to arithmetic.
sentences.zh: 左半球更倾向于将道德问题简化为算术题。

sentences.en: For example, if you, and this experiment has been done, if you disable temporarily the right temporoparietal junction,
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你——并且这个实验已经做过了——如果你暂时禁用了右侧颞顶联合区，

sentences.en: which you can do with a painless procedure, and ask people to solve moral problems,
sentences.zh: 你可以通过一种无痛的程序做到这一点，然后让人类去解决道德问题，

sentences.en: they give quite bizarre answers to them based on entirely utilitarian understanding of them.
sentences.zh: 他们会给出相当古怪的答案，这些答案完全基于对这些问题的功利主义理解。

sentences.en: An example is, a woman is having coffee with her friend.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，一个女人在和她的朋友喝咖啡。

sentences.en: She puts what she thinks is sugar in her friend's coffee, but it's in fact poison, and the friend dies.
sentences.zh: 她把她认为是糖的东西放进了朋友的咖啡里，但实际上那是毒药，然后朋友死了。

sentences.en: Scenario two, a woman is having coffee with her friend who she hates.
sentences.zh: 情境二，一个女人在和她讨厌的朋友喝咖啡。

sentences.en: She wants to poison her, and she puts what she thinks is poison in the coffee, but it's sugar, and the friend lives.
sentences.zh: 她想要毒死她，并把她认为是毒药的东西放进咖啡里，但实际上那是糖，然后朋友活了下来。

sentences.en: Which was the morally worst scenario?
sentences.zh: 哪个是道德上最糟糕的情境？

sentences.en: Now, all of us using our intact brains say, well, the one in which she intended to kill her friend.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们所有大脑完好的人都会说，嗯，当然是她意图谋杀朋友的那一个。

sentences.en: But, no, if you disable the right hemisphere, the good old left hemisphere says, well, obviously the one in which she died.
sentences.zh: 但是，不，如果你禁用了右半球，老实巴交的左半球就会说，很显然是她死掉的那一个。

sentences.en: So, values are not well appreciated, I think, by the left hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为左半球并不能很好地理解价值观。

sentences.en: One of the most striking differences between the hemispheres is how they relate to each other.
sentences.zh: 左右半球之间最显著的区别之一是它们彼此关联的方式。

sentences.en: With its big picture view of the world, the right hemisphere can see what the left hemisphere is doing, see the value that it produces.
sentences.zh: 凭借其对世界的宏观全景视角，右半球能够看到左半球在做什麽，并看到左半球所产出的价值。

sentences.en: But the left hemisphere, with its narrow view of reality, doesn't recognize the value of the right.
sentences.zh: 但左半球以其对现实的狭隘视角，却无法认识到右半球的价值。

sentences.en: In other words, the left hemisphere not only sees a narrow view of the world, it believes that the narrow view that it sees is all there is to see.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，左半球不仅对世界持狭隘观点，而且它还坚信自己所看到的狭隘观点就是全部的世界。

sentences.en: Ian explains this through one exchange between a physician and a patient who experienced right hemisphere brain damage.
sentences.zh: 伊恩通过一位医生与一位右脑受损患者之间的对话解释了这一点。

sentences.en: Her left hemisphere is still intact.
sentences.zh: 她的左半球仍然完好无损。

sentences.en: The patient has a strange belief about her own arm.
sentences.zh: 这位病人对自己的手臂有一种奇怪的信念。

sentences.en: How on earth does it happen to be here?
I found it in my bed.
sentences.zh: 我在我的床上找到它的。

sentences.en: How long has it been there?
The other day, too, when the weather was colder, it was warmer than mine.
sentences.zh: 前几天天气更冷的时候，它也比我的暖和。

sentences.en: I asked Ian how the patient could be unaware of her own arm and why she came up with this odd way to explain the presence of the arm attached to her.
sentences.zh: 我问伊恩，为什么这位病人会意识不到自己的手臂是自己的，以及为什么她会想出这种离奇的方式来解释附在她身上的手臂的存在。

sentences.en: Well, what we're seeing is a phenomenon called denial, which is a feature of the way the left hemisphere works.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们看到的是一种被称为否认的现象，这是左半球工作方式的一个特征。

sentences.en: So if you have a left hemisphere stroke, so your right hemisphere is still functioning, you're very aware of what deficits you have.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你发生了左半球中风，你的右半球仍在运作，你就会对自己的缺陷有非常清晰的认知。

sentences.en: If you have a right hemisphere stroke, you are completely unaware of there being anything wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果你发生了右半球中风，你则完全不会意识到有任何不对劲的地方。

sentences.en: So if you have a paralyzed left arm, which is often a consequence of right hemisphere stroke, more often than not, you will deny that there's any problem with it.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你有一只瘫痪的左臂（这通常是右半球中风的后果），十有八九你会否认它有任何问题。

sentences.en: If asked to move it, you will say there, but it didn't move.
sentences.zh: 如果被要求移动它，你会说动了，但它其实根本没动。

sentences.en: If, on the other hand, I bring it in front of you and say, whose arm is this?
sentences.zh: 另一方面，如果我把它拿到你面前并问：这是谁的手臂？

sentences.en: They say, oh, that's not mine.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，哦，那不是我的。

sentences.en: That belongs to you, doctor, or to the patient in the next bed, or as in this cut, my mother.
sentences.zh: 那是你的，医生，或者是隔壁床病人的，或者就像这次剪辑里说的，是我母亲的。

sentences.en: It's extraordinary because these are not people who are in any way mad.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了，因为这些人根本不是疯子。

sentences.en: They don't have a psychosis, but they're simply incapable of understanding that there is something wrong here that involves them.
sentences.zh: 他们没有精神病，但他们就是无法理解这里存在着涉及他们自身的问题。

sentences.en: When we look at patients who have damage not now to the right hemisphere, but to the left hemisphere, do we see a pattern in terms of how they behave, what deficits they have,
sentences.zh: 当我们观察那些受损部位不再是右半球、而是左半球的患者时，我们在他们的行为方式、他们有什么缺陷、
以及他们能够做什么方面，能看到某种规律吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it's really fascinating because the consequences are so obvious.
sentences.zh: 是的，这真的很迷人，因为后果太明显了。

sentences.en: You can't speak, and sometimes you can't appreciate the structure of a sentence that's being said to you.
sentences.zh: 你无法说话，有时你无法理解别人对你说的句子的结构。

sentences.en: The other thing that happens is you can't use your right hand, which is a bit of a bummer if that's your important hand.
sentences.zh: 发生的另一件事是，你无法使用你的右手——如果那是你重要的手的话，这就有点糟糕了。

sentences.en: But, effectively, the structure of reality is not changed.
sentences.zh: 不过，实际上，现实的结构并没有改变。

sentences.en: That's why it is easier to rehabilitate somebody after a left hemisphere stroke than after a right.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么左半球中风后的康复比右半球中风后更容易。

sentences.en: The left hemisphere is the one that sees body parts, whereas the right hemisphere is the one that sees the body as a whole.
sentences.zh: 左半球是看到身体各个部位的半球，而右半球则是把身体作为一个整体来看待的半球。

sentences.en: It has something called the body image, which is not just a visual image, but an integrated image from all senses of the body.
sentences.zh: 它有一个叫做身体意象的东西，这不仅仅是一个视觉图像，而是来自身体所有感觉的综合图像。

sentences.en: But I've been looking at all the interesting neuropsychiatric syndromes, many of them described by Oliver Sacks,
sentences.zh: 但我一直在研究所有有趣的神经精神综合征，其中许多是由奥利弗·萨克斯描述的，

sentences.en: which follow brain damage, and all these quite extraordinary, delusional, hallucinating syndromes that most people can hardly believe can happen to a human being
sentences.zh: 这些综合征伴随着脑损伤，所有这些非常罕见的、妄想的、产生幻觉的综合征，大多数人几乎不敢相信会发生在人类身上，

sentences.en: happen either only or very largely after damage to the right hemisphere, not after damage to the left.
sentences.zh: 它们发生在大面积损伤右半球之后，而不是在损伤左半球之后，或者主要发生在右半球损伤之后。

sentences.en: So, the succinct answer is the left hemisphere is to do with functioning and utilizing, reading, writing, and grasping.
sentences.zh: 所以，简而言之，左半球与功能、利用、阅读、写作和抓握有关。

sentences.en: And it doesn't really deal with the structure of reality, whereas the right hemisphere does.
